title: Redesign tone anchoring and introduce variable radius scale for components
creator: Elena Kim
body:
Summary:
We need a cohesive approach to color tone anchoring and a new variable radius scale that supports both standard and compact densities. Current token sets are inconsistent: some components hardcode surface tones and radii, which causes visual drift when density or brand palette changes. This ticket scopes the design work to define: a) semantic tone anchors for surfaces, borders, and interactive states across light/dark and high-contrast palettes, and b) a variable radius token system allowing responsive radius values and a migration map for components and patterns.

Goals:
- Define 6 semantic tone anchors (surface-0..surface-5) with clear mapping to product intents (background, card, elevated, interactive, overlay) and explicit contrast targets vs text and icons.
- Create a variable radius scale (radius-0..radius-5) that supports compact, default, and relaxed density variants and is easy for engineers to consume as CSS vars and JSON tokens.
- Ensure tokens are accessible: target WCAG AA for body text and AA+/AAA where feasible for controls. Provide contrast test fixtures and a small automated checklist.
- Produce design artifacts (Figma components + token spec) and a migration guide for engineers including aliases and a rollout plan that minimizes visual churn.

Scope (in-scope):
- Token definitions: color ramps for light/dark/high-contrast, alpha overlays, and elevation shadow presets tied to semantic surfaces.
- Radius scale: variable tokens, usage examples for buttons, cards, inputs, and menu surfaces.
- Acceptance criteria and test cases for contrast and density.
- Migration notes and token aliases for backward compatibility.

Out of scope (this ticket):
- Full implementation work in the runtime. (ENG tickets will consume the spec).
- Rework of iconography, spacing scale beyond radius, or complete component redesigns.

Proposed solution:
1) Tone Anchors: Introduce semantic names: surface-0 (app background), surface-1 (page card), surface-2 (control background), surface-3 (interactive/background highlight), surface-4 (modal/overlay), surface-5 (glassy/elevated). For each anchor define HSL base, neutralized versions for dark mode, and a 3-step contrast ramp for text/icons (normal, muted, disabled).
2) Radius Scale: Define radius-0..radius-5 as numeric tokens with conditional overrides: radius-*-compact, radius-*-default, radius-*-relaxed. Provide CSS variable examples and usage conventions: inputs and toasts use radius-1, cards radius-2, modal radius-4, and buttons radius-1 or radius-2 depending on density.
3) Shadows/Elevation: Replace ad-hoc shadow presets with semantic elevation tokens (elevation-0..elevation-4) mapped to shadow, blur, and overlay alpha. Tie elevation tokens to surface anchors so elevated surfaces automatically pick appropriate background and contrast.
4) Migration & Aliases: Keep deprecated tokens for two releases behind aliases (e.g., card-bg -> surface-1) and provide a codemod checklist and PR template.

Acceptance criteria:
- Figma token file published with light/dark/high-contrast variants and annotated examples for 12 core components.
- Design review completed with PM and Eng leads and feedback tracked.
- Contrast report attached demonstrating AA compliance for body text and interactive controls.
- Migration guide and token alias table created and stored in Confluence with example GitHub PR snippets.

Artifacts & Links:
- Figma token file: https://www.figma.com/file/REDACTED/design-system-tokens (internal)
- Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DS/pages/52345/Tone+Anchors+and+Radius+Scale (internal)
- Example PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/PR-NUM (replace with real PR on implementation)

Stakeholders:
- Design: Ava Moreno (lead), Elena Kim (owner)
- Engineering: Miguel Torres (runtime), Priya Shah (console)
- Product: Rohan Patel

Rollout plan:
Phase 1 (spec + design signoff): publish token spec, review with Eng (this ticket).
Phase 2 (pilot): implement tokens in Console shell components (header, sidebar, card). Close collaboration with ENG-1984.
Phase 3 (migration): component-by-component rollout with aliases and deprecation schedule.

Risks & Trade-offs:
- Risk: Surface token renames could cause subtle visual differences across customer UI. Mitigation: keep aliases and a two-release deprecation window, provide a visual diff checklist.
- Trade-off: More semantic tokens increase cognitive overhead but improve long-term consistency. We favor semantic clarity for cross-platform parity.

Next steps:
- Gather accessibility contrast numbers for proposed anchors (task assigned to Ava).
- Run a quick visual survey across 6 high-traffic pages to identify high-risk components.
- Schedule design review with Eng leads (done: 2025-11-07, see activities).

2025-11-07: Design review with Eng leads (Miguel, Priya). Agreed to keep alias layer for two releases; ENG-1984 and ENG-2050 added as dependencies.
2025-11-08: Added compact radius variants and example CSS variable usage to Figma file.
2025-11-10: Accessibility pass started — Ava to deliver contrast report by 2025-11-12.
2025-11-12: Design sign-off meeting notes added: accepted semantic anchors, asked for explicit shadow token mapping; action item for team to draft migration codemod examples.
